content: S ponsored Capitol Hill Auto Service , the Best of D.C. 2026 winner of Best Auto Repair! “We Don’t Just Work On Cars, We FIX Them.” Home | The Needle | Fall Arts Guide For 45 years, Washington City Paper has been here for D.C. And we’re not going anywhere. Since 1981, we’ve shown up with questions and curiosity to cover politics, people, neighborhoods, arts, and food with the local—and opinionated—perspective that has defined City Paper nearly half a century. Today, in celebration of our 45th anniversary, we’re kicking off our year-end campaign to raise $58,000 by Dec. 31 to keep this work going strong in 2027. Will you help us make sure City Paper is here for the next 45 years? Yes, I love WCP! The sun is shining (for now), the countdown to a four-day weekend is ticking, and some of us are still recovering from the Washington Spirit ’s brutal loss on Saturday night. Yes, it’s officially Monday in D.C. Here’s the news you may have missed while mourning the passing of longtime Washington Post book critic Jonathan Yardley , who died on Friday at the age of 87 . Suicide watched A recently amended wrongful death lawsuit filed by Dominique Watson in 2023 accuses the city and D.C. Jail for her husband’s death by suicide. According to court filings, a corrections officer told Giovanni Love , “I do not give a f—, kill yourself,” after Love said he was considering self-harm. The Post reports that Love died the following afternoon in 2022. Watson, whose suit accuses the District of negligence, says the city “spent years trying to shield the identity of the officer who allegedly spoke to Love,” which prevented her from adding the officer—only recently identified as Sunday Samuel Akanbi —as a defendant. That changed in October when U.S. District Judge Beryl A . Howell ruled that Akanbi could be added as a defendant to the suit. Howell wrote in her ruling that the “delayed production of the most early evidence collected by the District itself in internal investigation interviews … troubling, to say the least.” In memoriam Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George was among the mourners who gathered in Logan Circle on Saturday to remember James “ Jimmy ” Stuart , according to Axios . A member of D.C.’s gay community and longtime member of VIDA Fitness, the 46-year-old was killed on Nov. 12 in a shooting that took place inside and outside the gym and injured five others. “We believe that no one should have to carry the weight of tragedy alone,” VIDA president Aaron Moore said as neighbors, VIDA employees, and first responders joined hands and together passed a kettlebell between one another. Foundry United Methodist Church joined the memorial by ringing its bells for 46 seconds. Off to the races Ankit Jain is making a bid for Robert White ’s recently vacated seat on the D.C. Council. On Thursday , the city’s shadow senator announced that he was running for the at-large seat in the April 6 special election. The winner will serve the two remaining years of White’s term; White resigned last month in order to be the D.C. Delegate . — Sarah Marloff (tips? smarloff@washingtoncitypaper.com ) Last week’s trending stories: Before You Sign That Lease: A New Website Ranks D.C.’s “Worst Landlords” , Jennifer Hijazi Brings Loose Lips Back to City Paper Page Three Our regular column from staff photographer Darrow Montgomery . Building blocks : On Friday, U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema blocked construction of convicted felon and President Donald Trump ’s 250-foot arch indefinitely in the lawsuit brought by the Arlington County Board. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan had already blocked it through Dec. 3, but Brinkema’s ruling puts a serious damper on the president’s plans. During the hearing in Alexandria, Brinkema called Trump’s project a “rushed job.” Plus 10 points for indefinite blocks. +10 [ PBS News , MS Now , Reuters ] One man’s trash : Trump may have tried to close East Potomac golf course, but golfers are doing their best to keep it playable. Several days after the administration closed the course, locals started taking care of the place that Trump calls Trash Island. The golfers suing the government over Trump’s plans were at the park, which is still accessible and free, with real flagsticks, cups, and flags that were donated by another course. Plus two points for local love. +2 [ Post ] Revealed : A Metro rider inadvertently revealed a draft plan for firings and big changes at the National Museum of American History. In late October, an Orange Line commuter noticed a document titled “Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” on someone’s laptop, snapped a pic, and sent it to ProPublica . The 25-item list showed the plan to fire NMAH Director Anthea Hartig and a dozen others, end DEI, issue new guidelines, install exhibitions called The Riches of Our Western Civilization Inheritance and Great Families of American History , and install a “Colossus Statue” of George Washington . ProPublica believes the laptop belongs to Sam Bock , associate policy adviser with the Domestic Policy Council. Minus one point for secret plots to ruin the Smithsonian but plus one point for public tips. 0 [ ProPublica ] Dissent is patriotic : Air Force Maj. Jason Watson is being held in solitary confinement after criticizing Trump on CNN. “Not only is [Trump] a failure as president, he is flagrantly violating the Constitution, breaking the law, engaged in rampant corruption, and is killing Americans,” Watson told CNN in August. Watson was arrested at a protest in July at the U.S. Capitol where he held a sign calling for Trump to be removed from office while wearing his military uniform. The administration charged him under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and wants to keep him in isolation until his February trial. Watson’s attorney says he’s the first major in military history to be charged for “contemptuous words.” A ruling is expected soon. Minus one point for keeping a decorated officer in prison for speaking his mind. -1 [ Intercept ] Detained : Eva Yi Xie , a Princeton neuroscience student from China, was detained by ICE at National Airport on Nov. 19 after presenting her research at a conference. Her attorney says her family came to the U.S. when she was 14 and has had an asylum application pending for a decade, adding that the student has permission to live, work, and study in the U.S. Princeton’s graduate school dean and others are advocating for her return. Minus one point for detaining students who are allowed to be here. -1 [ Post , NBC4 ] Friday’s Needle rating : -77 Today’s score: +10 Today’s Needle rating: -67 By Gail O’Hara (tips? gail@washingtoncitypaper.com ) Chef Spike Mendelsohn ( Good Stuff Eatery , PLNT Burger ) opens his first stand-alone location of PLNT Cafe —a new plant-based spot serving up burgers, tacos, salads, and more—today in Mount Vernon Triangle. [ Washingtonian ] Guides to Union Station and all three D.C.-area airports for your Thanksgiving travel plans. [ City Cast DC , Eater ] The Big Stick is coming back to Navy Yard . Sorta. One of the shuttered haunt’s former owners is opening the Stick , a tavern with classic American eats, in the former Chicken + Whiskey space next year. [ WBJ ] By Samantha Ostwald (tips? sostwald@washingtoncitypaper.com ) More than four decades ago, Golshah Agdasi and her two children left Iran with the help of Kurdish smugglers. For the past 30 years, the artist has been a staple of Eastern Market. [ Hill Rag ] Local hardcore band NØ MAN gets some serious love from Polish journalist Karol Kamiński . The four-piece released their fourth full-length album, Between the Sword and the Neck , in October. [ IDIOTEQ ] For anyone still planning to tune in to the Kennedy Center Honors, CBS will air the awards ceremony on Dec. 27 at 8:30 p.m. The event takes place at Capital One Arena on Dec. 7. [ CBS ] By Sarah Marloff (tips? smarloff@washingtoncitypaper.com ) Sign up : To get District Line Daily—or any of our other email newsletters—sent straight to your mailbox, click here .
